ArgumentMap.title: ArgumentMap
ArgumentMap.description: Represents a saved argument analysis history for a user.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to manage user data, argument maps, and sources within the Argument Atlas application, while adhering to the core design principles of Authorization Independence, Clarity of Intent, DBAC (Database-Based Access Control), and QAPs (Rules are not Filters). It uses denormalization to ensure security rules can be evaluated without `get()` calls, and segregates data based on access control needs. User data and associated entities (ArgumentMaps, Sources) are stored under user-specific paths (`/users/{userId}`).

Authorization Independence is achieved by storing all user-owned data under the /users/{userId} path. This eliminates the need to perform `get()` calls in the security rules to verify ownership. QAPs are supported by limiting `list` operations to the user's own data or using membership maps to explicitly control access to shared data.

The `/users/{userId}` collection stores user profiles.  The `/users/{userId}/argumentMaps/{argumentMapId}` and `/users/{userId}/sources/{sourceId}` collections store user-created content.  This structure enables path-based ownership, simplifying security rules and improving scalability.
